text:
The last time most people saw Jack Hughes in a big moment, he was scoring the overtime winner for the United States in the Olympic gold medal game against Canada. Eighteen games into the Devils' season, he looks like a player who brought that feeling home.

Hughes has 25 points (9 goals, 16 assists), the Devils won nine of his last ten games, and he carries a five-game point streak, capped by the breakaway overtime winner on Long Island that finished a comeback from two down.

What makes this convincing is the process. At five on five the Devils take 65% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, ten points better than without him. His own chances are up to 1.69 expected goals per 60, from 1.05 last season, and he has actually scored a little under them. His linemates are finishing hot, so the assists may slow; the shot quality is real.

We'd watch the carries. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him bringing the puck in with control on 58% of his entries last season. That is how this offense starts.
headline: Jack Hughes is driving everything in New Jersey
